summary.headline: Shakti Pumps Q2 FY27: solar EPC revenue ~INR543 crores on 23,865 pumps installed (+7% YoY), with PM-KUSUM 2.0 approval still pending.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 solar pump installations of 23,865 units, up about 7% YoY, and cited roughly 70% growth across rooftop, solar domestic and industrial businesses. Q2 solar EPC revenue was about INR543 crores and exports about INR95 crores, with H1 solar EPC at about INR1,230 crores and H1 exports at INR177 crores. Margins were squeezed: raw material costs rose about 3% QoQ, offset by about 2% cost reduction, leaving EBITDA down about 1% QoQ. Working capital worsened, with about INR400 crores of collections slipping from Q2 into October, lifting debt to about INR830 crores before falling below INR500 crores. The call centred on the delayed PM-KUSUM 2.0 approval and the start of 500 MW solar panel trial production.

segments.name: Solar pumps (government and EPC)
segments.commentary: Q2 solar EPC revenue of approx. INR543 crores on 23,865 installations; H1 solar EPC approx. INR1,230 crores. Magel Tyala orders executed in Q2, with a 100,000-pump tender expected next quarter; 25,000-pump allocation in the latest market-mode tender was capped at 25% by an ADB condition.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q2 exports approx. INR95 crores; H1 exports INR177 crores including Uganda project. Middle East exposure is being offset by new markets; logistics handled by air freight where needed.

segments.name: Rooftop and solar domestic/industrial
segments.commentary: Management cited approx. 58% YoY rooftop revenue growth and approx. 70% growth across rooftop, domestic and industrial businesses. Rooftop volumes are constrained until Shakti-branded panels from the 500 MW plant are available.

segments.name: Solar cells and modules (500 MW panel plant, 2.2 GW cell plant)
segments.commentary: 500 MW panel facility has started trial production, with commercial production expected in 1 to 1.5 months. The 2.2 GW cell plant is about INR200 crores spent and due for completion in FY28, with strong revenue after March 2028.

guidance_outlook: PM-KUSUM 2.0 approval is expected in Q3 FY27, with execution results anticipated in Q4 FY27; management declined to give a firm launch date.
Management said the order book can cover Q3 FY27, with KUSUM 2.0 and Magel Tyala orders to add from next quarter; the company stated an order book of INR750 crores to be executed within 90 days.
Total FY27 capex plan is INR1,700 crores; approx. INR400 crores is expected in H2 FY27.
Debt is expected to decline further by March 2027, and collections to improve by year-end.
EBITDA guidance withheld until KUSUM 2.0 price list and tender rates are clear; margin benefit from the 500 MW panel plant expected to be visible next quarter but not yet quantified.
capex_capacity: Pump and motor facility under QIP 1 capex is underway; VFD and structure facilities are complete.
500 MW solar panel plant has started trial production; commercial production expected within 1 to 1.5 months.
2.2 GW solar cell plant: approx. INR200 crores spent to date; completion scheduled for FY28.
Pumps and motors capacity utilisation approx. 68% in H1 FY27.
Management said pump installation capacity will be expanded to speed up execution of new orders.
demand_pricing: Pricing flexibility is limited in solar, which is the majority of sales; only one active tender, concentrated in one state under Magel Tyala, and competitors chase the same opportunity.
Management said rates did not decline in the latest tender and expects rates to improve as bidders recognise that low quotes offer no advantage in market-mode tenders.
Raw material prices (MS, steel, copper) rose on the Strait of Hormuz conflict; management expects stabilisation.
Karnataka: approx. 12,000 pumps installed; management claims approx. 40% market share after late entry.
Export growth depends on geopolitical developments over the next six months; Uganda phase two funding is being requested from India Exim Bank.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins improve steadily, and can EBITDA be strong next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to guide EBITDA until KUSUM 2.0 price lists and tender rates are known; raw material costs rose about 3% QoQ, offset by about 2% savings.

qa_highlights.question: Can the revenue break-up for Q2 and H1 be provided?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2: solar EPC approx. INR543 crores, exports approx. INR95 crores, domestic/industrial/others approx. INR40 crores. H1: solar EPC approx. INR1,230 crores, exports INR177 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt and receivables rise, and where will debt end the year?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores of collections were received in October, not Q2. Debt was approx. INR830 crores, now below INR500 crores, expected to fall further by March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the solar cell and panel capex, and total FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: 500 MW panel line in trial production; 2.2 GW cell plant has approx. INR200 crores spent, due in FY28. Total FY27 capex is INR1,700 crores, with approx. INR400 crores in H2.

qa_highlights.question: If KUSUM 2.0 is delayed, what will utilise capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to Magel Tyala orders in hand for next quarter, a 100,000-pump tender, and open-market cash sales of solar pumps.

qa_highlights.question: Why was realisation flat, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation was roughly flat, with about 1% impact from sales mix. Management expects improvement but would quantify it only after the next tender price is derived; the ADB condition capped the company at 25,000 pumps in the latest tender.

risks_watch: PM-KUSUM 2.0 approval timing: management has repeatedly moved expectations, and it has been awaited for about six months.
Working capital: receivables of approx. INR1,750 crores and delayed ADB-linked payments; watch whether debt stays below INR500 crores by March 2027.
Raw material inflation (MS, steel, copper) linked to the Strait of Hormuz conflict, with pricing flexibility limited in solar tenders.
Execution of the 500 MW panel plant (approvals, licences, testing) and whether rooftop revenue scales as management expects.
Geopolitical impact on export markets, especially the Middle East, and dependence on the Uganda project.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations, volumes and the solar panel and cell roadmap, but cautious and often non-committal on KUSUM 2.0 timing, EBITDA and realisation, repeatedly deferring numbers to the next tender.
key_quotes: Despite challenging international conditions and logistics constraints in certain markets, we honoured our commitments to dealers and customers, using air freight wherever necessary.
Our margins depend on selling prices and raw material costs, which increased by approximately 3% quarter on quarter.
The order book we have needs to be completed within 90 days, and we are confident of executing it within that timeframe.

We established the 500 MW solar plant with the objective of expanding margins, but the benefits will not be immediate as approvals, licences, testing, and operational stabilisation are still underway.
